layers.name: Core
layers.description: The root layer every design system extends. It values the vocabulary: the palettes, the color roles drawn from them and the per-state rules of the components. It leaves no component out; a system chooses its components in its own layer.

neutral.description: Surfaces, text and the monochrome primary. Zero chroma.

accent.description: Tanrei's one chromatic voice: the keyboard focus ring. Declared by this system rather than fixed in the vocabulary, because which accent a product has — or whether it has one — is that product's choice.

error-quiet.description: The hue of the error palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The error palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

success-quiet.description: The hue of the success palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The success palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

warning-quiet.description: The hue of the warning palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The warning palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

info-quiet.description: The hue of the info palette at a low chroma: the faint tint a message of that status stands on, and the deep tone of what is drawn on it. The info palette keeps its full chroma for the status color itself.

syntax-keyword.description: A purple: the language's own words — its keywords, its modifiers, its at-rules. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-string.description: A green: text quoted in the code. It is near the hue of the success palette and is not that palette: a system that re-values success does not move it, and no status role reads it. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-constant.description: An orange: the values that are not text — numbers, booleans and null, named constants, units. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-function.description: A blue: the names of functions, and at a tone nearer the text, of properties. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-type.description: A blue-green: the names of types. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

syntax-tag.description: A red: what markup and style sheets address — an element's name, a selector. It is near the hue of the error palette and is not that palette: a system that re-values error does not move it, and no status role reads it. Declared by this system without roles: it colors code and nothing else.

tanrei.comp.menu.selected.container.colo.reason: A checked row is told by its mark, the check or the control look, which a person reads as the choice; at standard contrast it is drawn with no fill, as the menus of macOS, iOS and Fluent 2 draw theirs, so that the one row with a fill is the row the person is on (the current link item). A person who asks for more contrast is given the fill as a second cue: at medium and high contrast the row is a layer of its own content color, twice the hover layer, seen by the same step on whatever the sheet is and as far from a hovered row as a hovered row stands from one at rest.

tanrei.comp.menu.current.container.color.reason: The current link item has no mark: its fill alone tells the row the person is on from its neighbours, in every contrast scheme. The neutral palette's secondary-container is a tone chosen against the page: on the menu's lifted sheet it is 1.06:1 in dark, and in light the same grey as a hovered row.

tanrei.comp.list.selected.container.colo.reason: A selected option's fill is a layer of the row's own content color, twice the hover layer, as the menu's current link item is (and its checked row at medium and high contrast), so that the quiet selection looks the same in a list and in a menu and stands as far from a hovered row as a hovered row stands from one at rest. The neutral palette's secondary-container is a tone chosen against the page: in light it is the same grey as a hovered row (1.01:1 between them).

tanrei.comp.tree-view.selected.container.reason: A row's selection is the same layer in every component that selects rows: it follows tanrei.comp.list.selected.container.color, a layer of the row's own content color twice the hover layer, so that a selected node stands as far from a hovered one as a hovered one stands from one at rest. dial.$description: Dials: the few numbers a whole system is derived from. Change one and every token derived from it follows on every platform; tokens marked fixed do not. Color seeds are not dials — they are palette declarations in tokens/systems/.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Seven numbers the whole system is derived from. To make everything larger, roomier, rounder, bolder or slower, change a dial in your layer file instead of editing the tokens derived from it.
rules: Set a dial with {"$value": …, "reason": "…"} in a layer; never in component code.
A color is not a dial: declare or re-seed a palette under "palettes".
